skill.name: supabase-security-audit
skill.description: Review Supabase row level security policies and look for server-only credentials in browser code. Interpret squirrelscan findings and draft migration fixes for review.
skill.summary: Review Supabase access policies, flag exposed credentials, and draft fixes.
skill.author: squirrelscan
skill.license: See LICENSE file in repository root

security_audit.summary: The installer executes unverified remote code, and the skill directs agents to run an online audit and inspect files that may contain secrets. The workflow needs clearer controls for target authorization, cloud publication, database changes, and incomplete coverage. Most other alerts are Markdown syntax, links, or examples; no evidence of prompt injection or deliberate credential theft was found.

remediation.issue: The README pipes an unverified remote installer into a shell.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the pipeline with a pinned release and independent signature or checksum verification before execution. Require explicit approval before installing dependencies.

remediation.issue: The live audit can select a Supabase project discovered in site assets.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit approval of both the site and each exact Supabase project before making live requests. Stop if discovery identifies a project outside that scope.

remediation.issue: The signed-in workflow combines billing, publishing, and possible recurring audits.
remediation.suggestion: Separate consent for charges, report publication, dashboard enrollment, and scheduling. Default to unpublished reports and review all output for sensitive details before sharing.

remediation.issue: Framework environment files can contain privileged credentials.
remediation.suggestion: Check variable names and browser exposure without displaying values. Restrict any necessary reads to approved project files and redact secrets from logs and reports.

remediation.issue: Explained skips can satisfy the documented stop condition.
remediation.suggestion: Keep skipped checks marked unverified. Require a separate review of uncovered database objects and unresolved checks before declaring the access review complete.

remediation.issue: The suggested database changes lack a staging and approval gate.
remediation.suggestion: Draft versioned migrations and review the intended grants for each application role. Require staging checks and explicit approval before changing production policies.

semantic_findings.title: Discovered project is not explicitly bound to authorized scope
semantic_findings.description: The skill asks about ownership, then discovers the Supabase project from site scripts. Site authorization does not necessarily cover a project embedded in those scripts.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The workflow does not explicitly require matching the discovered project to a user-approved identifier. The documentation alone does not establish the CLI's runtime checks.

semantic_findings.title: Billing and report publication share an ambiguous consent step
semantic_findings.description: Signed-in audits may publish an unlisted report, add the site to a dashboard, and enable recurring audits. The workflow explicitly asks for approval of cost without separating those other decisions.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The skill discloses signed-in side effects and offers opt-outs. Its example does not select a private mode or show approval for each side effect.

semantic_findings.title: Incomplete checks can satisfy the stop condition
semantic_findings.description: The workflow allows closure after explained skips, even if table access was never checked. This can leave unresolved exposure when the audit is used for release sign-off.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The result guidance correctly treats skips as unchecked. The stop condition still permits closure without requiring a separate review of those gaps.

semantic_findings.title: Database policy changes lack an explicit approval gate
semantic_findings.description: The skill lists the SQL editor as a place to apply policy fixes. Enabling row level security without validating existing role access can interrupt normal application use.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The skill gives a sample policy and names the SQL editor. It does not require staging validation or explicit approval before applying production changes.

content.value_statement: Broad database policies and server-only keys in frontend code can expose private data. Review the code, interpret audit findings, and draft fixes before changing production.
actual_capabilities: Flags references to server-only Supabase keys in code that ships to browsers.
Identifies tables named in client code and checks migration files for matching access policies.
Interprets squirrelscan findings and distinguishes reported exposure from checks that did not run.
Drafts migrations that enable row level security and define access for intended roles.
Recommends rotation for exposed keys and documents approved public-table exceptions.
limitations: Live checks require squirrelscan, network access, and authorization for the target.
The live rule covers only tables identified in fetched scripts. Views, remote procedure calls, and other tables require separate review.
A zero count can mean that a table is empty or that anonymous users cannot see its rows.
Draft policies require schema-specific review and staging validation before production use.

use_cases.title: Review a frontend before release
use_cases.description: Check whether client files reference server-only credentials and report affected files without exposing key values.

use_cases.title: Review database policy coverage
use_cases.description: Match tables used by the client to migration policies and prepare changes for maintainer review.

use_cases.title: Triage a redacted Supabase audit report
use_cases.description: Separate observed exposure from skipped checks and assign follow-up reviews before release.

prompt_templates.title: Check frontend credential references
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the local frontend for references to server-only Supabase keys. Report file paths and variable names only. Do not print values, contact the app, or make changes.

prompt_templates.title: Check access policy coverage
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Review client queries and local migrations.
prompt_templates.prompt: List the tables referenced by the client and compare them with local row level security policies. Mark missing policies and unclear access rules. Use only local files.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize an existing audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this redacted Supabase audit report. Separate observed public access, approved exceptions, inconclusive counts, and skipped checks. Do not contact the site or database.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a migration for review
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: Prepare policy changes for a staging review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use these migrations and role requirements to draft narrower Supabase policies. Identify assumptions and describe staging checks for intended access. Do not connect to the database or apply changes.

output_examples.input: Review our frontend for references to server-only Supabase keys.
output: Finding: A browser entry point references the service role key. No credential value is included.
Recommendation: Move the privileged operation to the server and rotate the exposed key.

output_examples.input: Summarize this redacted audit for release review.
output: Public access: The report observed anonymous access to profiles. Review its intended audience and row level security policy.
Coverage gap: The orders check was skipped. Its access status remains unverified.
Exception: Posts is public by design and has an approved exception.

output_examples.input: Review the profiles migration and draft a policy change.
output: Proposed change: Limit profile reads to the owner and keep administrative requirements separate.
Review needed: Confirm which column identifies the owner and check expected access for each role in staging.
Status: Draft only. No database changes were applied.

best_practices: Review local migrations and credential references before authorizing a live check.
Redact key values and keep reports private unless sharing is approved.
Validate policies in staging with the application roles that need access.
anti_patterns: Approving a live check without confirming authorization for both the site and its Supabase project.
Treating zero counts or skipped checks as proof that access is restricted.
Applying a sample policy to production without verifying ownership and intended role access.

faq.question: Can I start without a deployed site?
faq.answer: Yes. Review client code and migration files locally without contacting a site or database.

faq.question: Is a Supabase publishable key a leaked secret?
faq.answer: No. It is intended for browsers. Service role and secret keys belong on the server because they can bypass row level security.

faq.question: Does a live check retrieve database rows?
faq.answer: The documented rule checks status and row counts without retrieving row contents. Live checks still require explicit target authorization.

faq.question: Does a passing result cover every table?
faq.answer: No. It covers only checked tables found in client scripts. Unlisted tables, views, and remote procedure calls still need review.

faq.question: Can signed-in audits publish results?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented signed-in mode can publish an unlisted report and incur charges. Review publishing settings and recurring audit options before running it.

faq.question: How should I handle the suggested migration?
faq.answer: Treat it as a draft. Check it against your schema and application roles, then validate it in staging before approving deployment.
